definitions.gloss: internal; in-house; relating to the inside of an organization or system
definitions.explanation: Describes something confined to the inside of an organization, group, system, or entity — as opposed to being external or public. Commonly used in business, legal, and technical writing to contrast with {外部的|がいぶてき} ('external').

examples.japanese: {内部的|ないぶてき}な{問題|もんだい}だ。
{内部的|ないぶてき}に{処理|しょり}してください。
この{件|けん}は{会社|かいしゃ}の{内部的|ないぶてき}な{事情|じじょう}によるものです。
examples.english: This matter is due to internal circumstances of the company.

examples.japanese: {政府|せいふ}は{内部的|ないぶてき}な{検討|けんとう}を{重|かさ}ねた{上|うえ}で、{最終|さいしゅう}{判断|はんだん}を{下|くだ}した。
examples.english: The government reached a final decision after repeated internal deliberations.

notes:
A na-adjective formed by attaching the suffix {〜的|てき} ('-ic; pertaining to') to {内部|ないぶ} ('interior; inside; the internal part'). It marks something as belonging to the internal sphere of an organization, system, or entity.

USAGE:
Strong bias toward formal, written, or business contexts. In everyday speech, {内部|ないぶ}の (using the noun directly with の) is often more natural; {内部的|ないぶてき} adds an abstract, categorical nuance ('of the internal kind').

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {内部的|ないぶてき}な{問題|もんだい}: an internal issue
- {内部的|ないぶてき}な{事情|じじょう}: internal circumstances
- {内部的|ないぶてき}{要因|よういん}: internal factor
- {内部的|ないぶてき}に{処理|しょり}する: to handle internally
- {内部的|ないぶてき}{対立|たいりつ}: internal conflict
- {内部的|ないぶてき}{検討|けんとう}: in-house review

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {内部|ないぶ}: interior; inside — noun; used as {内部|ないぶ}の + noun
- {社内|しゃない}: within the company — more specific, corporate
- {内|うち}{向|む}きの: inward-facing — suggests closed-off attitude rather than category
- {外部的|がいぶてき}: external — the direct antonym

CONTRAST WITH {内部|ないぶ}の:
- {内部|ないぶ}の{問題|もんだい}: an internal problem (concrete, factual)
- {内部的|ないぶてき}な{問題|もんだい}: an internal-type problem (categorical, often contrasted with external)
The difference is subtle, but {〜的|てき} adds an abstract, classifying feel suitable for formal analysis.
